summary: Specializing in Indology, history, and archaeology, James Wilkinson Breeks studied at the East India Company College around 1850 to 1852. He subsequently served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1852 until 1872.

James Wilson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1870–1873) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1873–1875). He worked as a civil servant in the Indian Civil Service from 1873 to 1910.

Linguist James Wilson Bright earned his undergraduate degree at Lafayette College (~1873–1877) and his PhD at Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1882). He taught at Cornell University (~1884–1885) and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins (1905–1925).

Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught figures such as Shenphen Nangwa and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge studied under the 16th Karmapa, Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, and Kalu Rinpoche in 1973. He taught Richard Barron and Jampa Mackenzie Stewart.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye studied under masters including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1840–1892), Tai Situ Pema Nyinje Wangpo, and Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa. He taught figures including Karma Tashi Chophel and Khakyab Dorje.

Jamie Hubbard, a specialist in Buddhist studies and Japanology, studied at Komazawa University and completed a PhD under Minoru Kiyota at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. At Smith College, he held the Yehan Numata and Jill Ker Conway professorships (attested 2016–2026).
Active in Tibetology and linguistics, Jampa Lhundup studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and served on its faculty as Assistant Professor of Art History (attested 2026).

Scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies Jampa Losang Panglung earned a Geshe Lharampa at Sera Monastery (-1958) and degrees at the University of Munich (~1968–1979). He worked at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1979–2006), including on its Tibetan dictionary.
Jampa Mackenzie Stewart, active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, completed his traditional studies under Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Jampa Samten worked as a bibliographer at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 1987) and served at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as Director (attested 2003–2004) and Professor (attested 2015–2026).
Specializing in Tibetology, Jampal Kunzang Rechung served as Deputy Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1982) and edited the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1980–1988).

Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Kalu Rinpoche, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and Tsennyi Tulku Jampal Norbu. He taught the 14th Dalai Lama and the 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche.

A figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö succeeded Dzongsar Khyentse Jamyang Chökyi Wangpo. He studied under masters including Shechen Gyaltsab and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and taught Namkhai Norbu, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Sogyal Rinpoche.

A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo studied under numerous teachers including Rigdzin Zangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye. He taught prominent figures including Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Jamyang Sherab Chokyi Nangwa pursued traditional studies under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Indologist Jan A. Schoterman earned his degrees, including a PhD under Henk Bodewitz (1982), at Utrecht University, also studying under Jan Gonda. He held posts at Utrecht University, Tilburg University, and the Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies.

Jan Brunson, working in Indology, earned a PhD from Brown University in 2008. She was a Visiting Assistant Professor at Bowdoin College (2008–2011) and held an Affiliate Faculty appointment at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 2011.

Indologist and religious studies scholar Jan C. Heesterman completed his doctoral studies under Jan Gonda (~1953–1957). He served as a Professor at Leiden University from 1964 to 1990, succeeding F. B. J. Kuiper in 1972.

Jan Chozen Bays studied under Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada after earning degrees from Swarthmore College and UC San Diego. Working in Buddhist and religious studies, she taught at Zen Community of Oregon (1985) and served as abbess of Great Vow Zen Monastery (~2002).
